Name: Ruin Abilities
Description:
Vessel of Ruin (284), Sword of Ruin (285), Tablets of Ruin (286) and Beads of Ruin (287) - byte-for-byte transcription of a modder's (ABZB) own verified ARM research (Ruin Abilities.xlsx), two shared functions reused across all four ability ids.

IDs verified this session via cfg.GetText(TextName.AbilityNames) against the real ROM, not guessed: Intrepid Sword=234, Dauntless Shield=235, Seed Sower=269, Thermal Exchange=270, Purifying Salt=272, Guard Dog=275, Good as Gold=283, Vessel of Ruin=284, Sword of Ruin=285, Tablets of Ruin=286, Beads of Ruin=287. None of the four Ruin ids had an existing ability-master-table entry before this package (map.Find(Ability,id) == null for all four), so this is new installation, not a duplicate of native code. All four ids also fall inside the separate 216-slot high-id ability dispatcher's gate-bitmask range (ids 234-329, table at 0x110538) but that dispatcher is a DIFFERENT, unrelated mechanism (used natively only by Electromorphosis/Wind Power/Wind Rider/Protosynthesis/Quark Drive per walkthrough.md); this package uses the same plain ability-master-table + Timing-slot path already proven working by CudChew.json/Ripen.json/TarShot.json, which needs no gate-bit changes.

FUNCTION A - 'report self' (switch-in ability banner), installed once at SourceBase 0x107DCC, referenced by every ability at Timing 0x6D AND Timing 0xA7 (both switch-in-family timings; 0xA7 is independently confirmed as a live 'entry' timing by Protosynthesis/Quark Drive's native routine at 0x113CA0 per walkthrough.md). Logic: if the Pokemon whose ability this is IS the one that just triggered (checked via 'bl 0x87B58' GetBattleVar(0x2)==self), show the ability-activation banner with self index + ability-name text variables, then hide it. Every one of its 6 BL targets (0x87B58, 0x89E28, 0x876F8, 0x89C6C, 0x7F804, 0x7CCF4) was independently re-disassembled against the real Battle.cro and confirmed to be real function prologues; 0x87B58/0x92298/0x876F8/0x7CCF4/0x89E28 are the exact same targets already cross-verified as live, working code by the CudChew.json session (228-2070 independent BL callers found elsewhere in this ROM for each). 0x89C6C and 0x7F804 are new to this package: both sit immediately after a 'BX R14' at a clean function boundary and have 322 and 385 independent BL callers respectively elsewhere in Battle.cro, consistent with small bitfield text-variable setters. No PC-relative literal loads (LDR Rd,[PC,#imm]) anywhere in this function, so CodeRelocator.RebaseCode's branch-only fixups are sufficient if the installer places it somewhere other than 0x107DCC - no CudChew-style ADD-PC fix needed.

FUNCTION B - 'decrease stat of others', installed once at SourceBase 0x107E5C, referenced by every ability at Timing 0x4A AND Timing 0x4B. r9 holds the CURRENT TIMING (0x4A or 0x4B, matching the section title and both literal comparisons exactly; ability ids 74/75 make no sense here since the four real Ruin ids are 284-287, so r9=ability-id was ruled out). Logic: reads the stat category being calculated (r7, via ldrh [r0,0x38] minus 0x100), asks whether it's a physical or special stat (bl 0x87B58 GetBattleVar(0x1E)), then via r9/r7 selects exactly one of the four abilities (Vessel->SpA r7=0x1C, Tablets->Atk r7=0x1E, Sword->Def r7=0x1D, Beads->SpD r7=0x1F) and excludes the ability holder itself from its own debuff (self-not-attacker / self-not-defender checks via GetBattleVar(0x3)/(0x4)). All of this control-flow logic re-disassembled cleanly with every branch landing on a real instruction boundary (verified via ARMCodec.Disassemble at the real target address).

DISCLOSED DEVIATION (the one change from ABZB's raw bytes, same spirit as CudChew.json's ADD-PC fix): the donor's last stretch (get ability-holder pointer via bl 0x92298, then 'bl 0x00101970' to count how many Pokemon on the field share this exact ability, then pick a diminishing-returns multiplier - 0xC00/0xDC0/0xE60 Q12.4 fixed point - for 1/2/3+ instances) could NOT be verified against this exact ROM build: 0x101970 has ZERO independent BL callers anywhere else in Battle.cro (checked by scanning every BL in the whole 0x15C000-byte file), and a 0x180-byte disassembly window around it (0x101900-0x101A80) shows it lands in the middle of an unrelated, unbroken chain of CMP/LDREQ/MOVEQ comparisons with no push/pop function boundary nearby - the opposite of what CudChew's Pickup cross-check or this same package's other 8 BL targets showed. Calling it as written would jump into the middle of someone else's lookup table with no matching return path - a hang/crash class bug, exactly what SAFETY RULE 6 exists to catch rather than ship on ABZB's stated comment alone. Rather than fabricate a replacement address, the single 4-byte instruction 'BL 0x00101970' (9EE6FFEB) at 0x107EF0 is replaced with a NOP (0000A0E1, the same 'MOV Rd,Rn' encoding already used verbatim elsewhere in this exact function, e.g. row 26/82 of the source spreadsheet, just with Rd=Rn=r0). Nothing else shifts - same instruction count, same length, every other byte and every branch target in the function is untouched. Net effect: R2 (party count, set to 1 by the unmodified preceding 'MOV R2,#0x1 include self' instruction) is left at 1 instead of being overwritten by a real per-side count, so the subsequent CMP R2,#0x2 / MOVCC R1,#0xC00 always takes the 'exactly 1 instance' branch and applies the flat, verified-correct 0.75x multiplier via the confirmed-live 0x83108 dispatcher (independently confirmed as this ROM's real damage/stat-multiplier engine by the already-shipped, native-verified Fickle Beam proc in walkthrough.md, which calls the exact same address). Practical effect: correct behavior whenever at most one Pokemon per side has a given Ruin ability (the overwhelmingly common case, and the only case in singles); if 2+ Pokemon on one side ever share the exact same Ruin ability simultaneously (only possible in doubles/triples with a duplicate-ability team), each instance will independently apply the flat 0.75x rather than the real games' smoothed diminishing-returns curve, so duplicate stacking is slightly harsher (naive multiplicative 0.75^n) than mainline. Flagged here rather than silently shipped; the real per-side ability-count helper for this exact ROM build is unresolved and would need Julien to re-derive it (or confirm ABZB's own build differs at 0x101970) before the diminishing-returns refinement can be restored byte-for-byte.
